title: Not the same
review_text: I've been wearing 510's for the last 8 years and I am very disappointed to say that these are NOT the same jeans that I fell in love with. I'm so disappointed with these new "510's" and unfortunately I'm going to have to look elsewhere for something that resembles the old "super skinny" fit. 1/10 would not recommend if you're looking for an actually skinny jean.

title: Awful
review_text: I've worn 510s and 511s for a long time, and I've always loved them. But I just bought a new pair of 510s, and they're terrible. As others have mentioned, the crotch sits way too low, and the quality of the denim is extremely poor. These jeans are too stretchy, and they do not fit comfortably against the leg. Instead, they sag. The old 510s were fantastic, but these stretch denim versions are not worth it. I'll not buy these again until Levis goes back to the old 510s

title: Jet Color Has Strange Fit
review_text: I ordered a bunch of 510's at once and the Jet color definitely has something wrong with the fit for this batch. They are tight up top and very tight and the knee, but the cut from the knee down is boxy and a little strange. Not the worst pants ever, but not as sleek as a normal 510. I do hope Levi's will fix this in future versions of the black 510. The Coral, Winetasting and Westside colors all have a more traditional 510 cut.

title: Bummer Levi's
review_text: I've worn EXCLUSIVELY the 510 Skinny Fit (jet) Jeans for years now. I loved them- note the shift to past tense. I too have noticed the gradual decline in the quality of these jeans. Just as everyone is saying here: the waist is higher, the crotch lower, the ankle doesn't taper to a skinny fit let alone a super skinny fit- which I think this inconsistency between one pair to the next bothers me the most. I'd also agree the overall hand of the denim has gotten pretty bad. The color of the denim is pretty whack as well- definitely not Jet Black throughout- the reverse side of the denim has a yellow tint, which looks pretty terrible if you like to cuff your jeans. All these inconsistencies in one pair of 510's to the next has completely exhausted me. Buying a pair of 510's has become a tiresome hunt where I have in the past tried on four pairs of the same size just to try and figure out which one wasn't the worst fit, but I'm done doing that. I've concluded they are all pretty bad. Bummer Levi's.

title: Not the same 510 at all...
review_text: Not the same as they use to be. These do not fit anywhere close to my previous pairs of 510's. I was excited to see my favorite cut back again in my size, but now I'm back to having to shop elsewhere.

title: Buy 511's + Taper them from the thigh down
review_text: These jeans are awful. The leg opening is wide, the thighs are incredibly tight, and the crotch drops low. 511's however still feel pretty good in the waist, crotch and thighs. I just bought a couple pairs and took them to a tailor and had her slim them into what the old 510's were. Sure it is an annoying extra step, but it worked.

title: Not So Skinny
review_text: These appear to be Levi's skinniest model, which is pretty shocking. They're just not skinny. They're relatively close down to just above the knee but from there down they just aren't. At all. I'm 5'9", 170 lbs., so I'm not a toothpick. I don't need these to fit like stretch pants or cut off my circulation, but there shouldn't be a lot of material floating around that you can just grab, which is the case the full length of these jeans. The leg opening should be awfully close to my leg but it's not even pretending. I could literally fit the leg opening easily over cowboy boots, if I were inclined to wear cowboy boots, which I am not. I can hold a full 2" flap from the leg opening to the calf - that's not a skinny fit by any definition. They don't look tapered, they look boxy. My wife walked in while I was trying them on and she literally said, "Are those Husky Cut or what?". I want to wear Levi's because I like the quality, but I don't think I can deal with these. I bought two pair and they're both the same. They're just bad. I guess I'll have to find some generic brand that understands, as Levi's did at one time, how skinny jeans are supposed to fit.

title: Baffled by New Fit; Levis Missed the Mark
review_text: I agree with the others who believe Levis messed up with the new fit. Seriously, what were they thinking? The crotch sits way too low, so it feels like you're "sagging" your pants even if you're wearing them where they naturally fall on your waist. The openings are not tapered enough and feel weird. After a few washes, I've found that the legs shrink in length, so you'll be pulling the leg bottoms down every time you stand up. I've owned a couple pairs of these revised 510s and will not be buying another unless Levis listens to the complaints. They tried to go too middle of the road and failed. I loved the old "super skinny" fit, never had a problem with them shrinking, and the material felt better.

title: 510 became old 511
review_text: What happened Levi's? The 510 super skinny were my go to jeans of choice for years now. Unfortunately it looks like the one pair I have left is the last i'll own. title: Better quality control needed. These are slim fit and sometimes that may be generous.
review_text: Seven pairs of Levi 510's in Jet later, and I now know that quality control is almost absent from this particular fit. They are generally okay around the waist, but the leg is not actually skinny on most of them. These do not have a consistent fit. I have pairs in 32x34 that are WAY skinnier than the ones in 30x30. How? Probably because quality control is lacking. I know I am far from the first person to complain about this.

title: Strange fitting
review_text: I have purchased few 510's, Levi keeps on changing the fit of these. Secondly, the current fit available hangs too low in the crotch at least 1.5 inches extra. This restricts your movement which is not expected from a jean because you wear jean to move freely. If you pull the jeans up and wear a tighter belt, it doesn't look smart at all. I would say, only a super skinny guy should wear these.

title: Why did Levi's change the fit?!
review_text: I recently purchased these jeans in a Levi's store and was GREATLY disappointed. I'm 5'6" 140-145lbs. with and athletic/muscular build and typically wear my 510s a size 30x32. As others have noted the color is misleading in the photo. The wash is a bit darker than it appears online in person. Upon trying the new fit/style on in the store I went doen 2 sizes in the waist while my length remained the same. However after taking the jeans home and wearing/walking around in them a bit longer, I noticed that the crotch sags. I measured it and the seam (zipper to where the stitching meets) is 2" larger than normal which makes for a awkward fit. Also the material feels a bit thin and less durable. I really hope they go back to the measurements, materials, and sizing previously used. Levi's typically does such great work. It's unfortunate they changed. I'm hoping a tailor can make the necessary adjustments to the crotch in the jeans to fix the overall fit.

title: No longer skinny

The long crotch, high cut and looser fit no longer fit my body type, and as such I'll not buy another pair again. Why change the cut of a classic jean, Levis? LEAVE IT ALONE - IT WAS JUST FINE!

title: Redesigned!!! Not As Skinny!!!
review_text: I'm 6'0", 32x30, and I've been wearing 510's religiously for the past 2 years+. But when I ordered a new pair in Jet last week, I noticed some elements had been redesigned (for the worse, IMO). There was a weird bunching of material around the knee, and around the leg opening- more space, I assume, they're trying to give you. I was immediately skeptical. The waist seemed ok at first, but as it stretched over a few wears, it become much too large (falling off my butt, actually). I checked out the label and noticed a new material they're using. It used to be 98% cotton, 2% spandex. Now, it's 2% "elastine". Whatever. Eventually I went to a store and tried on a whole waist size lower- 31" (I've never worn this size in anything)- and discovered this was the trick for getting the true 510 fit! So...tight pants haters...rejoice, because you don't have to order a size up anymore- Levis has it built in for you! For us tight pantsed rock stars, order a size down to get the look you used to know and love!
